area_description: Making, supplying and approving sustainable aviation fuel.

idea_types.name: SAF production
idea_types.description: Making sustainable aviation fuel from waste, plants or other sources, for example turning used cooking oil into jet fuel.
also_called: used cooking oil to jet fuel

rules.document: ASTM D7566 - Specification for Aviation Turbine Fuel Containing Synthesized Hydrocarbons
rules.why_it_applies: The fuel standard a synthetic or bio-based jet fuel must meet before it can be blended and used.

rules.document: ASTM D4054 - Practice for Evaluation of New Aviation Turbine Fuels and Fuel Additives
rules.why_it_applies: The route a new fuel follows to be tested and approved for aircraft use.

rules.document: ASTM D1655 - Specification for Aviation Turbine Fuels
rules.why_it_applies: The base standard for the jet fuel that blends are mixed into and that airlines buy.

rules.document: CORSIA Eligible Fuels, including the CORSIA Sustainability Criteria and Life Cycle Assessment Methodology
rules.why_it_applies: Lists which fuels count under CORSIA and the sustainability and life-cycle rules they must meet.

rules.document: Sustainable Aviation Fuels (SAF) guidance and ICAO CAAF framework
rules.why_it_applies: Describes ICAO's framework for sustainable aviation fuels and how they are counted.

readiness_checklist: Description of the process and the fuel pathway
Feedstock source, quantity and how it is traced
Life-cycle emissions estimate with method
Plan to test the fuel against the standard
Production volume and timeline
Sustainability evidence for the feedstock
Who will buy or blend the fuel
reviewer_questions: Which approved production pathway does your process follow?
Where does the feedstock come from, and can it be traced?
How much lower are life-cycle emissions, and how were they calculated?
Has the fuel been tested against the standard?
How much can you really produce, and when?
idea_types.national_requirements: Check with your civil aviation authority for the national requirements that also apply.

idea_types.name: SAF feedstock supply
idea_types.description: Collecting or growing the raw material that sustainable fuel is made from, such as used oil, crop residue or waste.

rules.document: Environmental protection: aviation and the environment overview
rules.why_it_applies: Explains ICAO's environmental work and how its measures fit together.

readiness_checklist: Description of the material and its source
Quantity available each month or year
How collection and storage work
Evidence that it does not harm food, land or forests
Traceability records
Quality checks
Buyers or fuel producers you can supply
reviewer_questions: Where exactly does the material come from?
Does collecting it compete with food or damage land?
How can a buyer verify its origin?
Which fuel producers could use it?
